summary: Pend Oreille County, WA: a 14x14 ft cabin (1929) was replaced by a 40 ft L-4 tower (1934); the tower was removed in the 1960s and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 14 x 14 ft log and frame cabin (1929), replaced in 1934 by a 40 ft L-4 tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and Willhite say the tower was removed in the 1960s, and Forest Lookouts marks the site as removed. FireLookout says it was destroyed in the 1960s. The story reports removal as the majority account and notes the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Access and present condition are not described by any source read, so the brief's access 'unknown' stays unset. The Walker and Hawk anecdote is undated on the page. Willhite says the mountain was named in honor of 'one of these men' without saying which; Ole Jackson is only the surname match, and the story says so. The FFLOS 1933 photo has no image URL in the cached text, so no photos were added.
